q: 1. In a stair the most suitable position to provide winders is ..........
explain: Winders are tapered steps used to change the direction of a stair without a landing. They are safest and most commonly placed at the start (bottom) of a flight.

q: 2. The height of hand railing above the tread should be generally between ..........
explain: For ergonomic comfort and safety, handrails are typically fixed at a height of 750 mm to 800 mm (75-80 cm) above the line of nosing.

q: 3. The best spacing of timber piles from center to center is ..........
explain: A spacing of 900 mm (or 3 times the diameter) is generally recommended for timber piles to ensure proper group action and soil stability.

q: 4. A horizontal member of stone, concrete or wood provided to give support for the vertical member of a wooden window, is called ..........
explain: The sill is the horizontal bottom member of a window frame that sheds water away from the wall.

q: 5. The exposed vertical surface left on the sides of an opening after the door or window frame has been fitted in position, is called ..........
explain: The reveal is the part of the side of a window or door opening that is visible between the frame and the outer surface of the wall.

q: 6. The noggin pieces are housed in the studs at a vertical distance of about ..........
explain: For structural stability in a brick nogging wall, horizontal noggins are spaced at intervals of 60 to 90 cm.

q: 7. The moulding provided under nosing to beautify the elevation of a step of stair, is called ..........
explain: Scotia is a decorative concave moulding often placed under the nosing of a tread for aesthetic appeal.

q: 8. A series of steps without any platform, break or landing in their direction, is called ..........
explain: A flight is an uninterrupted series of steps between floors or landings.

q: 9. The projecting part of the tread beyond the face of riser is called ..........
explain: Nosing is the edge of the tread that extends over the riser to provide more foot space.

q: 10. The angle which the line of nosing of the stair makes with the horizontal, is called ..........
explain: The pitch is the angle of inclination of the stairs, ideally between 25 and 40 degrees.

q: 11. In stairs, the vertical portion of a step providing a support to the tread, is known as ..........
explain: The riser is the vertical member between two treads.

q: 12. In residential building, the average value of stair width is ..........
explain: A minimum width of 900mm (0.9m) is standard for residential stairs to allow for a single person to move comfortably.

q: 13. The pitch of stair should never exceed ..........
explain: Stairs steeper than 40 degrees are difficult to climb and become dangerous; they are typically kept between 25° and 40°.

q: 14. In designing a stair, the sum of going (in cm) and twice the rise (in cm) should be equal to ..........
explain: The standard comfort formula is (2 * Riser) + Tread = 60 cm (approx).

q: 15. In designing a stair, the product of going (in cm) and twice the rise (in cm) should be equal ..........
explain: Another empirical rule for comfortable stairs is that Tread * Riser should be approximately 400 to 450 cm².

q: 16. The vertical members which support the door frame are called ..........
explain: The vertical sides of a frame are referred to as posts (or jambs in some contexts), while styles are the vertical members of the door leaf itself.

q: 17. The external jamb of a door or window opening at right angles to the wall face, is called ..........
explain: Reveals are the vertical sides of an opening that are exposed between the frame and the wall face.

q: 18. A horizontal member of a frame employed to sub-divide a window opening horizontally is called ..........
explain: A transom is a horizontal bar of wood or stone across a window or door.

q: 19. The width of jambs is ..........
explain: Standard jamb width for typical door frames ranges from 7.5cm to 11.5cm.

q: 20. The depth of jambs is ..........
explain: The depth of the jamb or frame section is usually between 60mm and 75mm.

q: 21. The projections which help in securing the head of a door frame to the masonry, are called ..........
explain: Horns are the horizontal projections of the head and sill beyond the vertical posts to fix the frame into the wall.

q: 22. The window used with the object of providing light and air to the end closed space below the roof is called ..........
explain: A dormer window is a vertical window that projects from a sloping roof.

q: 23. The window usually provided near the main roof of a room and opens above the adjoining verandah, is called ..........
explain: Clerestory windows are located near the top of a wall, often above an adjacent roof level, to provide light and ventilation to the inner part of a room.

q: 24. A rigid formed by the intersection of two sloped surfaces having an exterior angle greater than 180°, is called ..........
explain: A hip is the external angle formed by the intersection of two sloping roof surfaces. An internal angle would be called a valley.

q: 25. The horizontal members of wood or steel used to support the common rafter of a sloping roof, are called ..........
explain: Purlins are horizontal structural members that span between trusses or walls to support the common rafters or roofing sheets.

q: 26. In a sloping roof, the inclined wooden members laid from the ridge to the eaves known as ..........
explain: Common rafters extend from the ridge to the eaves and provide the main support for the roof covering.

q: 27. The term pitch in connection with pitched roofs is defined as a ..........
options: apex line of the sloping roof
inclination of the sides of a roof to the horizontal plane
horizontal distance between the internal faces of the walls
triangular upper part of a wall formed at the end of a pitch roof
explain: Pitch is the numerical measure of the steepness of a roof, expressed as the ratio of rise to span or as an angle.

q: 28. A pitched roof in which rafters slope to one side only is called ..........
explain: A lean-to roof (also known as a pent or shed roof) consists of a single sloping surface, usually attached to a taller wall.

q: 29. The combination of a king-post truss and queen post truss is known as ..........
explain: A Mansard truss is a 'broken' roof truss that is steeper at the bottom and flatter at the top, effectively combining structural elements to maximize attic space.

q: 30. The coupled roof is suitable for spans upto ..........
explain: Coupled roofs are simple sloping roofs without a tie beam, making them unsuitable for spans exceeding 3.5 meters due to outward thrust.

q: 31. The type of truss commonly used for spans varying from 5 to 9 meter is ..........
explain: A King Post truss utilizes a single central vertical post and is most economical for spans in the range of 5 to 9 meters.

q: 32. In a queen post truss, ....... vertical posts are used.
explain: A Queen Post truss is distinguished by having two vertical tension members (posts) instead of one.

q: 33. A queen post truss is commonly used for spans ..........
explain: Because it has two vertical supports, the Queen Post truss is suitable for larger spans, typically 8 to 12 meters.

q: 34. A couple-close roof is used for spans up to ..........
explain: Adding a horizontal tie beam to a couple roof creates a 'couple-close' roof, extending the safe span to about 5 meters.

q: 35. The process of filling up all nail holes, cracks etc. with putty is known as ..........
explain: Stopping involves using putty or wood filler to smooth out surface imperfections before painting.

q: 36. A truss having upper and lower pitch, and made by combining king and queen post trusses, also used as a roof, is known as ...........
explain: A Mansard truss provides two different slopes on the same side, often utilized to create habitable attic space.

q: 37. The short piece of timber bolted to the rafters of a roof truss fixing the purlin in position are named as ...........
explain: Cleats are small blocks of wood or steel angles fixed to the principal rafters to prevent the purlins from sliding down.

q: 38. In the king post truss the member used to prevent the sagging of beam and connected with the ridge is called ...........
explain: The King Post is the central vertical tension member that 'hangs' from the ridge to support the center of the tie beam.

q: 39. A rolling shutter is often used for ...........
explain: Rolling shutters provide high security and occupy minimal space, making them the standard choice for storefronts (shops) and garages.

q: 40. In king post the number of vertical posts is ...........
explain: A King Post truss is characterized by exactly one central vertical post.

q: 41. Screws for wood work as specified by ...........
explain: Wood screws are commercially classified by their length and their 'gauge' (diameter of the shank).

q: 42. Keeping in view possibility of shrinkage and wrapping the width of the boards is recommended to be ...........
explain: Narrower boards (approx. 10 cm) are less prone to significant warping or 'cupping' compared to wider boards.
